items.definition:
a person who tries to undermine a political system
The government cracked down on suspected subversives.

a large, heavy book
He spent hours poring over ancient tomes in the library.

a person advocating a totalitarian system of government
The country was ruled by a totalitarian regime.

the highest point; a corner or point where lines meet
The vertex of the triangle was at the top.

fuss; trouble
They finished the project with much ado.

compliance with standards, rules, or laws
There was a strong pressure for conformity in the group.

a spouse, especially of a monarch
The queen and her consort attended the ceremony.

outward behavior or bearing
His calm demeanor reassured everyone during the crisis.

a short, ceremonial tune or flourish played on brass instruments
The arrival of the queen was met with a loud fanfare.

A right to keep possession of property belonging to another person until a debt owed by that person is discharged.
The bank placed a lien on the property until the loan was repaid.

A chronic autoimmune disease.
She was diagnosed with lupus after experiencing persistent fatigue.

A colorless fluid containing white blood cells, which bathes the tissues and drains through the lymphatic system into the blood.
The lymphatic system carries lymph throughout the body.

Inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord.
Meningitis can be a very serious infection.

Dislike of, contempt for, or ingrained prejudice against women.
The play explored themes of misogyny and gender inequality.

a fierce or destructive attack
The city prepared for the onslaught of the approaching storm.

paralysis, especially that which is accompanied by involuntary tremors
Cerebral palsy affects muscle control and coordination.

a force that is not part of a country's armed forces but is organized like an army
The government deployed paramilitary forces to maintain order.

the fact of happening again
Doctors are trying to prevent the recurrence of the illness.

the making of amends for a wrong one has done, by paying money to or otherwise helping those who have been wronged
The country demanded reparations for the damage caused during the war.

the ability to appreciate and respond to complex emotional or aesthetic influences
Her artistic sensibility was evident in her paintings.

a strong feeling of suitability for a particular career or occupation
She felt that teaching was her true vocation.

the process of taking in and fully understanding information or ideas.
The assimilation of new immigrants into society can be challenging.

an act of breaking away from a group or organization.
The breakaway group formed a new political party.

a picture, description, or imitation of a person or thing in which striking characteristics are exaggerated to create a comic or grotesque effect.
The artist drew a caricature of the politician.

a phrase or opinion that is overused and betrays a lack of original thought.
"Time heals all wounds" is a common cliché.

a territory or cultural group surrounded by a larger one
The small village was an artistic enclave within the bustling city.

a group of people attending or surrounding an important person
The celebrity arrived with her entire entourage.

a period of time in history or a person's life, typically one marked by notable events
The invention of the internet marked a new epoch in communication.

a woman (French loanword, often used in specific phrases like 'femme fatale')
She played the role of a classic femme fatale.

people of good social position, especially those of the class next below nobility
The local gentry owned most of the land.

The act of imposing something, especially a burden or unwelcome demand.
I hope my request isn't too much of an imposition.

A form or collection of forms of public worship.
The church's liturgy includes hymns, prayers, and readings.

the state of being famous or well known for some bad quality or deed
He gained notoriety for his controversial opinions.

the science dealing with X-rays and other high-energy radiation
She decided to pursue a career in radiology.

a temporary diminution of the seriousness or intensity of disease or pain
The patient's cancer went into remission after treatment.

the action of repenting; sincere regret or remorse
He showed deep repentance for his past mistakes.

the restoration of something lost or stolen to its proper owner; recompense for injury or loss
The court ordered him to make restitution to the victims.

a religious ceremony or ritual regarded as imparting divine grace
Baptism is an important sacrament in many Christian churches.

a person or thing that causes great trouble or suffering
The disease was a scourge on the population for centuries.

waste material from smelting
The furnace produced a significant amount of slag.

the state of not flowing or developing
Economic stagnation led to widespread unemployment.

a salt or ester of sulfuric acid
Copper sulfate is often used as a fungicide.

the scientific study of animals
He decided to major in zoology at university.

the practice of refraining from indulging in something
He practiced abstinence from alcohol for a year.

a person who is intolerant toward those holding different opinions
His comments revealed him to be a bigot.

gold or silver in bulk, typically in the form of bars or ingots
The bank vault contained stacks of gold bullion.

an official in a bureaucracy, especially one perceived as concerned with procedural correctness at the expense of people's needs
He complained about the slow process, blaming the bureaucrats.

A type of oil or bean; a star in Gemini
Castor oil is known for its various uses.

An ancient manuscript book
The ancient codex contained rare illustrations.

A type of drawing crayon
The artist used a conte crayon for the sketch.

The act of spreading widely
The dispersion of seeds was aided by the wind.

Intricate and delicate skill
He handled the delicate negotiation with great finesse.

A long, narrow inlet of the sea, especially in Scotland
The boat sailed into the firth.

the art or practice of garden cultivation and management
She studied horticulture at university.

exemption from punishment or freedom from the injurious consequences of an action
The criminals acted with impunity.

the state of being unable to pay debts
The company declared insolvency after heavy losses.

a particular position, point, or place
The brain is the locus of consciousness.

a type of skin cancer
Early detection of melanoma is crucial for successful treatment.

a prison for people convicted of serious crimes
He was sentenced to serve time in the state penitentiary.

a short period of rest or relief from something difficult or unpleasant
The rain offered a brief respite from the oppressive heat.

a derogatory remark or insinuation; an act of speaking indistinctly
He was accused of using a racial slur.

the final stop or destination in a transport system
The bus reached its terminus at the city center.

one of the two oval organs that produce sperm in male animals
The doctor examined the patient's testicles.

the amount of material or items passing through a system or process
The new machine increased the factory's throughput.
